cards.q: Where does most photosynthesis happen in a plant?
cards.a: In the leaves. All green parts have chloroplasts, but leaves are the main site.

cards.q: What gives leaves their green color?
cards.a: Chlorophyll - a light-absorbing pigment inside the chloroplasts.

cards.q: What is the main job of chlorophyll?
cards.a: It absorbs light energy so the plant can turn solar energy into chemical energy.
The green tissue inside the leaf where most chloroplasts are found.
Tiny pores in the leaf. CO2 enters and O2 exits through them. (Stoma = 'mouth')

cards.q: How does water get to the leaves?
cards.a: Roots absorb it, then veins carry it up to the leaves.

cards.q: How does sugar made in a leaf reach the rest of the plant?
cards.a: Veins carry it from the leaf to the roots and other parts.

cards.q: About how many chloroplasts does a mesophyll cell have?

cards.a: An envelope made of two membranes.
The thick fluid filling the chloroplast's inner compartment. Sugar is made here.
Connected membrane sacs inside the stroma. They enclose the thylakoid space.

cards.q: Where in the chloroplast is chlorophyll located?
Thylakoids vs stroma: who does what?
cards.a: Thylakoid membranes turn light energy into chemical energy. The stroma uses it to make sugar.

cards.q: How do CO2 and water reach the chloroplasts in a leaf?
cards.a: CO2 enters through the stomata. Water comes from the roots through the veins.
